name: TMP411ADGKR
title: TMP411 and TMP411D: remote and local temperature sensor, I2C/SMBus, with η-factor and series-resistance correction
summary: A digital thermometer with two channels: its own die temperature and an external PN junction (a discrete transistor or a processor's thermal diode) on D+ and D-. Results of up to 12 bits are read over I2C/SMBus at up to 3.4 MHz; programmable limits drive an ALERT/THERM2 output and a THERM output, both open-drain. Series resistance up to 3 kΩ is cancelled, the ideality factor is adjustable, and an open sensor is detected. TMP411 (VSSOP-8, SOIC-8; 2.7 V to 5.5 V) is ±1 °C and ships on a legacy or a new die; TMP411D (SOT-23-8; 1.62 V to 5.5 V) is ±0.8 °C. TMP411ADGKR is the VSSOP-8 part at address 4Ch.
key_figures: ±1 °C max (TMP411, TA 15 to 75 °C); ±0.8 °C max (TMP411D, TA -25 to 85 °C)

notes: The letter after TMP411 or TMP411D sets the bus address: A 4Ch, B 4Dh, C 4Eh, E 4Ch with the remote offset registers (11h, 12h). The package code follows: D is SOIC-8 (1.75 mm max height), DGK is VSSOP-8 (1.1 mm max), DDF is SOT-23-THIN-8 (1.1 mm max); R is a large reel, 2500 parts for TMP411 and 3000 for TMP411D. A Q1 suffix marks the AEC-Q100 automotive parts.

TMP411 A, B, C and E parts in D and DGK may carry either the legacy die (CSO WFM or DM5) or the new die (CSO RFB); the date code on the reel label tells which. TMP411D is built only on the new die (RFB).

pins.name: V+
pins.function: Supply input: 2.7 V to 5.5 V for TMP411, 1.62 V to 5.5 V for TMP411D. Decouple to GND with 0.1 µF.

pins.name: D+
pins.function: Positive side of the remote sensing junction (emitter of a PNP, or the tied collector and base of an NPN). Tie to D- when the remote channel is unused.

pins.name: D-
pins.function: Negative side of the remote sensing junction.

pins.name: THERM
pins.function: Active-low open-drain thermal flag; needs a pull-up to V+. Cannot be disabled by software.

pins.name: ALERT/THERM2
pins.function: Active-low open-drain alert output, or a second thermal flag when the configuration register selects THERM2; needs a pull-up to V+.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: Open-drain serial data for I2C/SMBus; needs a pull-up resistor.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: Serial clock input for I2C/SMBus; needs a pull-up resistor when driven open-drain.

circuits.title: Basic connections (transistor-connected PNP sensor)
circuits.description: The TMP411 on a 5 V rail reading a PNP transistor as its remote sensor. The emitter feeds D+ and the base feeds D- through optional matched series resistors, with an optional capacitor across the pair at the pins; the collector goes to ground. SCL, SDA, ALERT/THERM2 and THERM each have a 10 kΩ pull-up to the rail; the bus pins run to an SMBus controller and THERM to a fan controller. A 0.1 µF capacitor decouples V+.

parts.note: optional series resistor; under 1.5 kΩ in most designs, 50 Ω suggested for filtering
optional series resistor, same value as R1
optional; under 1000 pF in most designs, 100 pF suggested for filtering

notes: A transistor connection cancels series resistance better; a diode connection settles faster. NPN transistors are used diode-connected only.
The same connections apply to the TMP411D.

equations.name: Junction voltage difference
equations.expr: VBE2 − VBE1 = (n × k × T / q) × ln(I2 / I1)

where.n: ideality factor of the remote junction
where.VBE1, VBE2: base-emitter voltage at I1 and at I2

equations.note: The remote channel steps the junction through its excitation currents and converts this difference to temperature.

where.NADJUST: signed value in the N-factor correction register (18h), −128 to 127

equations.name: Correction value for a given ideality factor

where.neff: ideality factor of the chosen transistor

equations.note: The result is written in two's complement.

where.n: ideality factor of the remote junction (nactual)

equations.name: Temperature from the two register bytes (12-bit, Q4)
equations.expr: T(°C) = ((high << 8 | low) >> 4) × 0.0625; in extended range subtract 64
equations.note: The value is unsigned. Bytes 18h and 80h give 24.5 °C.

equations.name: Self-heating
equations.expr: ΔTJ = (V+ × IQ + IOL × VOL per output) × θJA

where.IQ: average supply current at the chosen conversion rate
where.IOL × VOL: power in each open-drain output that is sinking

equations.note: At 3.3 V and 8 conversions/s with ALERT/THERM2 and THERM each sinking 1 mA at 0.4 V: legacy TMP411 1.32 mW + 0.8 mW = 2.12 mW, about 0.318 °C rise with 150 °C/W; new-chip TMP411 0.149 mW + 0.8 mW = 0.949 mW, about 0.154 °C with 162 °C/W; TMP411D 0.949 mW, about 0.173 °C with 182 °C/W.

operation.text: One package holds a local die-temperature channel and a channel that reads an external PN junction (a discrete transistor or a thermal diode built into a processor, ASIC or FPGA). Results, limits and status live in registers reached over an I2C/SMBus target interface. High and low limits drive the ALERT output; separate THERM limits drive the THERM output for a system response to overheating. The pin-out and registers match the ADT7461 and ADM1032.

The remote junction is driven with stepped currents: 6 µA low and 120 µA high, with a 60 µA middle step (the legacy die also has 12 µA), so D+ steps through three levels during a remote conversion, typically between about 0.54 V and 0.62 V. The conversion assumes an ideality factor of 1.008.
Up to 3 kΩ of resistance in series with the remote junction (trace and cable) is cancelled automatically. Up to 1000 pF across D+ and D- changes the reading very little.

D+ and D- have an internal 65 kHz filter. A capacitor across the inputs, 100 pF to 1 nF, is advised against coupled noise. Series resistance can help in some setups and must stay at 3 kΩ or less. Where filtering is used, 100 pF and 50 Ω on each input is the starting point.

The default range is 0 °C to 127 °C in plain binary: readings below 0 clamp to 00h and above 127 to 7Fh. Setting RANGE (configuration bit 2) selects the extended range, −55 °C to 150 °C, where 64 (40h) is added to every value, starting with the next conversion. Values are not two's complement. The high byte holds whole degrees; the low byte holds the fraction in its top four bits. The remote channel always resolves 0.0625 °C; the local channel is set to 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 or 0.0625 °C. Limit registers are not rewritten when the range changes and must be reprogrammed in the new format.

Local results are at 00h (high) and 15h (low), remote at 01h and 10h; they are read-only and update after each conversion. Read the high byte first: a low-byte read in the very next command returns the same conversion. A two-byte read from 00h or 01h returns both bytes of one conversion.

Both outputs are open-drain, active low, and can be wire-ORed with other sensors. THERM goes low when either channel passes its THERM limit (local 20h, remote 19h, 1 °C steps, default 85 °C) and releases when the temperature falls back by the hysteresis in 21h (default 10 °C). In ALERT mode (configuration bit 5 = 0) pin 6 goes low when a channel leaves its high/low window for the number of consecutive conversions set in register 22h (1 to 4), or when the remote junction is open; MASK (bit 7) silences it. ALERT clears after an alert-response read returns this part's address, the cause has gone and the status register has been read. In THERM2 mode (bit 5 = 1) pin 6 behaves like THERM but uses the high limit registers.

Eleven read/write registers hold the limits. High and low limits span a high and low byte like the results: local high is written at 0Bh/16h and read at 05h/16h, local low written at 0Ch/17h and read at 06h/17h, remote high written at 0Dh/13h and read at 07h/13h, remote low written at 0Eh/14h and read at 08h/14h. Power-on values: high limits 55h (85 °C standard, 21 °C extended), low limits 00h (0 °C standard, −64 °C extended). The hysteresis value is unsigned and must be smaller than the limits it applies to, or the comparators never release on a falling temperature.

Register 02h holds BUSY, LHIGH, LLOW, RHIGH, RLOW, OPEN, RTHRM and LTHRM. LLOW, RLOW, OPEN, and LHIGH/RHIGH in ALERT mode latch until the register is read (and the cause is gone) or the part resets. BUSY, LTHRM, RTHRM, and LHIGH/RHIGH in THERM2 mode show the live state. In ALERT mode any of LHIGH, LLOW, RHIGH, RLOW or OPEN rising pulls ALERT low. Reading status does not release ALERT. With no remote junction and a supply ramp slower than 240 V/s, RLOW is set and should be ignored.

A comparator flags an open or miswired remote junction when D+ rises above about (V+) − 0.6 V during a conversion. The last good result is kept, OPEN (status bit 2) is set and ALERT goes low if enabled. Short D+ to D- when the remote channel is not used.

TMP411 only. The legacy die converts only once V+ exceeds about 2.45 V; between the POR level and that point it still answers on the bus and keeps the last result. On the new die the lockout is merged with power-on reset (about 1.23 V): above POR it both communicates and converts.

Setting SD (configuration bit 6) stops everything except the serial interface; shutdown current is typically under 3 µA (0.6 µA for the new die and TMP411D). Entering shutdown during the local conversion leaves both results unchanged; during the remote conversion the local result still updates. Clearing SD resumes continuous conversion at the programmed rate.

In shutdown, writing any value to 0Fh runs one conversion on both channels, after which the part returns to shutdown. Wait 200 µs after entering shutdown before the first one-shot; after that, one-shots can follow without delay. A shutdown command lets the conversion in progress finish.

Register 04h (written at 0Ah) sets 0.0625 to 8 conversions per second by changing the idle time between conversions, trading supply current against update rate. Local resolution (register 1Ah) changes the conversion time of the legacy TMP411 only; on the new die and TMP411D the local conversion is 17.7 ms at every resolution.

Register 18h holds a signed correction that changes the ideality factor used for the remote channel (default 1.008, power-on 00h). TMP411E and TMP411DE add an offset register (11h/12h, same format as the result) that is added to each remote result, for system calibration together with the ideality correction.
The part records the lowest and highest local and remote results since power-on, reset, or a write to any address from 30h to 37h. Minimum registers reset to FFh/F0h and maximum registers to 00h/00h.
Register FEh returns manufacturer code 55h; FFh returns the device ID (12h for A and E, 13h for B, 10h for C).

The part is a target only. SDA and SCL are open-drain with spike filters and Schmitt inputs. Fast mode runs from 1 kHz to 400 kHz and high-speed mode from 1 kHz to 3.4 MHz; data goes MSB first. Every write starts with the pointer byte; a read uses the last pointer written, so repeated reads of one register need no new pointer. Two-byte transfers send the high byte first.

To go above 400 kHz the controller sends the Hs-mode code 00001XXX after a START. The part does not acknowledge it but switches its input and output filters, then accepts transfers up to 3.4 MHz until the next STOP.

With bit 7 of register 22h set (the default), the interface resets if SCL or SDA is held low for about 30 ms between START and STOP, releasing the bus if the part was holding it. Keep SCL at 1 kHz or faster to avoid tripping it.

A general call (address 00h) followed by 06h, or a write of any value to pointer FCh, restores every register to its power-on value, aborts a running conversion and releases ALERT and THERM. Other second bytes after a general call are ignored.

When pin 6 is in ALERT mode and low, a controller sending the SMBus alert command (0001 1001) gets this part's address back; the last bit is 1 if a high limit caused the alert and 0 if a low limit did. If several parts answer, the one that wins arbitration releases its ALERT; the others keep theirs asserted.

With V+ at 2.7 V or more the logic thresholds are fixed (2.1 V / 0.8 V), so pins 4, 6, 7 and 8 may be pulled up to a separate bus supply. Below 2.7 V (TMP411D only) SCL and SDA thresholds track V+ (70 % / 30 %), so the pull-ups must go to the same supply as V+.

Best accuracy comes from a transistor with VBE above 0.25 V at 6 µA at the hottest temperature, VBE below 0.95 V at 120 µA at the coldest, base resistance under 100 Ω, and hFE held in a narrow band (50 to 150). The 2N3904 (NPN) and 2N3906 (PNP) meet this. NPN or PNP types both work, provided the sensing element is the base-emitter junction.

The local sensor follows the ambient air and the board; its thermal time constant is about 2 s, so a 100 °C step takes about 10 s to settle within 1 °C. Excitation current adds negligible heat; supply current and sinking outputs add some (see the self-heating equation).
The part is tuned for 3.3 V and stays accurate across its supply range. Place a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor right at V+ and GND; noisy or high-impedance supplies may need more.

Put the part as near the remote junction as practical. Run D+ and D- side by side with ground guard traces either side, and on multilayer boards between ground or supply planes; 0.127 mm traces are suggested. Match the number and placement of copper-to-solder joints in the two lines so thermocouple voltages cancel. Keep total capacitance across D+ and D-, including any cable, to 1000 pF or less. For links under about 20 cm use twisted pair; for longer ones use shielded twisted pair with the shield grounded only at the TMP411 end.
